name: ARRAYFORMULA
description: ARRAYFORMULA lets you apply a single formula to an entire range of cells automatically, expanding results into neighboring rows and columns without manually filling down or across.
tldr: ARRAYFORMULA wraps a formula and applies it to every cell in a range at once, so you don't need to copy formulas down.

parameters.name: array_formula
parameters.description: Any formula or expression that returns an array or range result. The formula is evaluated once for each row/column in the input ranges.

basicExample.description: Multiply two columns row by row using a single formula
basicExample.result: Column of products for each row
basicExample.explanation: Instead of writing =A2*B2 in C2 and copying down, ARRAYFORMULA calculates the product for every row in A2:A10 and B2:B10 in one cell.

advancedExamples.title: Conditional array with IF
advancedExamples.description: Calculate 10% commission only for sales greater than $1,000
advancedExamples.explanation: The IF statement is applied to each row. Only rows above $1,000 get a 10% commission; others return 0.

advancedExamples.title: Combine with FILTER
advancedExamples.description: Filter and transform a dataset in one formula
advancedExamples.result: Filtered rows with values increased by 10%
advancedExamples.explanation: FILTER returns qualifying rows, and ARRAYFORMULA applies the 10% increase to the numeric columns.

howItWorks: ARRAYFORMULA evaluates the inner expression for each element of the input arrays and returns a spilled array. Any range references inside the formula are iterated element-by-element. It works especially well with IF, mathematical operators, and functions that normally return scalar values.

howToSteps.name: Pick a scalar formula
howToSteps.text: Write a formula you would normally copy down, such as =A2*B2.

howToSteps.name: Replace ranges with arrays
howToSteps.text: Change the references to full ranges, e.g. =A2:A10*B2:B10.

howToSteps.name: Place in one cell
howToSteps.text: Enter the formula in a single cell and it will expand automatically.

limitations: ARRAYFORMULA is Google Sheets only; Excel uses dynamic arrays (e.g. =A2:A10*B2:B10 spills automatically).
Some functions like SUM, COUNT, or AVERAGE return a single value and do not spill inside ARRAYFORMULA.
If the output range overlaps existing data, the formula returns a #REF! error.

commonErrors.cause: The spilled array is blocked by existing data in adjacent cells.
commonErrors.fix: Clear the cells below or to the right where the formula is trying to expand.

commonErrors.cause: A function inside the formula is aggregating the result (e.g., SUM, COUNT).
commonErrors.fix: Use row-by-row equivalents or remove the aggregator; SUM cannot be arrayed directly.

commonErrors.cause: Input ranges have different numbers of rows or columns.
commonErrors.fix: Ensure all referenced ranges have the same dimensions.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: ARRAYFORMULA is native to Google Sheets. Excel 365 achieves similar behavior through implicit dynamic arrays without needing to wrap the formula.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: In Excel 365, =A2:A10*B2:B10 spills automatically. Older Excel versions require array entry (Ctrl+Shift+Enter).

faq.question: Can ARRAYFORMULA work with SUM?
faq.answer: No, SUM returns a single number. For row-by-row sums, use =ARRAYFORMULA(A2:A10+B2:B10) or =SUMPRODUCT(A2:A10, B2:B10).

faq.question: Why does ARRAYFORMULA return #REF?
faq.answer: The array is trying to expand into cells that already contain data. Clear those cells.

faq.question: Can I use ARRAYFORMULA with VLOOKUP?
faq.answer: Yes, but only if the lookup value is an array. For example: =ARRAYFORMULA(VLOOKUP(A2:A10, Sheet2!A:B, 2, FALSE)).

faq.question: Does ARRAYFORMULA slow down a sheet?
faq.answer: It can on very large ranges because the formula is calculated for every cell at once. For huge datasets, consider using QUERY or pivot tables.
